question: Should OpenClaw ship a today-only iOS capability that sends user-requested HealthKit aggregates through the Gateway to the configured AI provider under this disclosure and two-opt-in model?
rationale: Code can enforce a fixed read-only payload, but accepting sensitive health-data transfer, App Store privacy obligations, and the intended consent model requires explicit maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve bounded summaries
options.body: Accept the today-only aggregate after the overlap bug is fixed, signed-device proof is posted, and privacy/App Store disclosures are release-ready.

options.title: Keep HealthKit out
options.body: Do not ship the capability because transmitting health aggregates to model providers is outside the desired application privacy boundary.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded summaries
recommendation.body: Accept the today-only aggregate after the overlap bug is fixed, signed-device proof is posted, and privacy/App Store disclosures are release-ready.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal spans the affected iOS node, Gateway policy, signing, and mobile capability surfaces.
